history.title: Period ledger exceptions
history.intro: What does not add up in the workers' movement history in the old system, to review and fix there before the switchover.
history.how: After every sync each worker's period history is built from the old system: work starts, approved housing orders and approved vacations in date order; each movement starts a period that the next one closes (the day of a move belongs to the new period). From 2025, with the last movement before it as the starting point. Fixes are made in the old system, and the exception disappears at the next sync.

codes.OnJobWithoutWorkStart: On the job without a work start
codes.StatusMismatch: Status does not match the history
codes.ProjectMismatch: Project does not match the last work start

explain.SameDay: The worker has more than one movement on the same day (e.g. duplicate work starts). The latest created was kept; cancel the duplicate in the old system.
explain.Gap: A movement ended (end date) before the next one started, leaving days where nobody knows where the worker was (neither invoiced nor counted).
explain.EndBeforeStart: The end date of the work start or vacation is before its start; ignored.
explain.EndAfterNext: A movement's end date is after the next movement's start (overlap); the next one's start was used.
explain.WorkWithoutPrice: A work start without a service price, and no service price on the worker: its days cannot be invoiced.
explain.ReturnWithoutWork: A "returned worker" housing order while the history does not have the worker on a project before it.
explain.OnJobWithoutWorkStart: The worker is "on the job" in the old system without any work start to show it.
explain.StatusMismatch: The worker's status in the old system does not match the last movement of their history (e.g. last housed but on the job).
explain.ProjectMismatch: The worker is on the job on another project than their last work start.

invoiceCheck.title: Attendance vs invoices
invoiceCheck.intro: Each line of the old system's project invoices against the days and price in the period ledger for the same worker, project and invoice period.
invoiceCheck.how: The invoice's days are its working days (an absent day is still a day on the project, deducted from the amount); the ledger's days are the days of work periods on the project within the invoice's period (a fully covered period counts as the invoice's month days). An invoice belongs to the month it ends in; canceled ones are left out. The check starts in September 2026, the first month whose invoices were matched with the periods before being made. Rebuilt after every sync.
invoiceCheck.target: Target: 99% before the ledger is relied on for invoicing
invoiceCheck.search: Search by worker number or name, project or invoice number
invoiceCheck.none: No invoices to check yet; they appear after the next sync.

explain.Match: The same working days and the same monthly price.
explain.DaysDiff: The invoice's working days differ from the ledger's work days: a missing or wrong movement in the old system (work start, return or vacation), or days changed by hand on the invoice.
explain.PriceDiff: The same days at another monthly price, or a work start without a price in the ledger: check the work start's price in the old system.
explain.DaysAndPriceDiff: Both the days and the price differ.
explain.NotInLedger: The worker is invoiced on the project, but the ledger does not have them there in the invoice's period (e.g. in housing per the ledger).
explain.NotInvoiced: The ledger has the worker on the project, the project has an invoice for the month, but the worker is not on it.
explain.ProjectNotInvoiced: Workers on projects without an invoice for the month (internal projects such as head office, or an invoice not made yet). Not counted in the match rate.

numbering.title: Document numbering
numbering.intro: How each screen's documents are numbered: the number's pattern, when its counter starts again, and the number it starts from.
numbering.how: A pattern is fixed text with tokens: {N:5} is the running number on five digits, {YYYY} or {YY} the year, {MM} the month. E.g. DO-{YYYY}-{N:5} gives DO-2026-00001. "Start from" continues an old serial (e.g. worker number BSS002869) and never goes back to a number already issued. "Reserved" documents have no screen yet; set their serial now for when it is built.
numbering.patternHint: Click a token to add it at the end of the pattern.
numbering.startHint: To continue the old system's serial; numbers already issued never repeat.
numbering.resetWarning: Changing when the counter starts again starts a new counter from "Start from"; make sure the new pattern cannot give numbers already issued.

problems.pattern: The pattern needs {N} and known tokens only.
problems.year: A yearly counter needs the year in the pattern ({YYYY} or {YY}), or numbers repeat.
problems.month: A monthly counter needs the year and the month ({MM}) in the pattern.

timesheets.title: Monthly timesheets
timesheets.intro: Each project's timesheet for its billing cycle, generated from the period ledger. Approved, it makes the customer invoice, the payroll of the company's workers and each internal supplier's statement.
timesheets.projectMissingHint: The project is not in this system (created before 2025 or not brought over yet), so no timesheet can be generated.
timesheets.empty: No projects with work this month.
timesheets.noPrice: Workers without a price in their periods ({{workers}}): fix the price in the period ledger (or the old system), then generate again before sending.
timesheets.approvedHint: Approved ({{name}}) and locked: the customer invoice is made from it, the payroll takes the company's workers, and the supplier statements theirs.
timesheets.noLines: No work periods on the project in this cycle.
timesheets.noSuppliers: No suppliers' workers on this timesheet.
timesheets.payrollHint: The company's sponsored workers: what this timesheet pays. The payroll adds loans, penalties, internal additions and housing days later.
timesheets.suppliersHint: Internal suppliers' workers, by supplier: the worker's net the supplier pays. The supplier statement adds the supplier's fees and cost-card items.
timesheets.invoiceHint: The invoice this timesheet makes, item by item. The actual invoice (its number and ZATCA) is issued from the approved timesheet.
timesheets.unknownHint: Workers with no sponsor in the old system, so it is not known whether they are the company's or a supplier's: neither the payroll nor a statement takes them until their sponsor is set.

adjustmentHints.Absence: Off the salary part of the invoice and the worker's pay; the fees stay. Not more than the work days.
adjustmentHints.Overtime: By the project's rule (basic ÷ monthly hours × multiplier, or a fixed hourly rate); added to the invoice and the worker.
adjustmentHints.ClientAddition: A bonus or allowance the customer pays: added to the invoice and the worker.
adjustmentHints.ClientDeduction: A deduction the customer asks for: off the invoice and the worker.
adjustmentHints.CustomerLoan: A loan the customer paid the worker: off the invoice and the worker.
adjustmentHints.FeeDays: When fee days differ from work days (+ or −): the fee part only.
adjustmentHints.OtherCost: Another cost on the customer: invoice only.
adjustmentHints.InternalAddition: An amount the company adds to the worker (bonus, allowance): added to the worker's pay only, not to the invoice.
adjustmentHints.InternalDeduction: An amount the company deducts from the worker (penalty, a company loan): taken off the worker's pay only, never the invoice.
